semantic_uniqueness_method: Exact feature-name and product-scoped mechanism/workflow phrase screening against all inventory records; selected candidates are distinct in feature mechanism, transaction, failure class, evidence, question, and topology fingerprints.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Proxy-mode SSL inspection: strict HTTP conformance checks, ALPN negotiation, and HTTP/2 fallback
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Proxy-mode TLS interception forwards or strips ALPN from ClientHello according to supported-alpn; strict-web-check rejects nonconforming HTTP headers; HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 behavior is controlled independently.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client TLS ClientHello -> FortiGate proxy inspects/forwards ALPN -> upstream negotiates HTTP/2 or HTTP/1.1 -> decrypted HTTP headers pass strict web check -> proxy forwards response.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Proxy-mode deep-inspection compatibility failure producing HTTP 400 for selected origins.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Reproduction only under proxy mode with deep inspection; disabling strict-web-check changes behavior; supported-alpn http1-1 changes ClientHello ALPN forwarding; flow mode is unaffected in the reported case.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use a narrowly scoped proxy-policy/profile test; validate upstream HTTP/2/ALPN behavior; apply strict-web-check disable only when justified, or constrain ALPN to HTTP/1.1 for affected destinations; preserve flow-mode comparison and rollback.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Differentiate HTTP header conformance rejection from TLS certificate failure and choose the least-broad ALPN/strict-check test.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client -> FortiGate proxy inspection boundary -> upstream TLS server; annotate ClientHello ALPN, decrypted HTTP header validation, and 400 failure point.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiManager 8.0 granular admin-profile permissions for device configuration and routing
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Manage Device Configurations is split into Interface, Log & Report, Security Fabric, Others, plus Routing and SD-WAN permissions; the new permission model controls device configuration menu and provisioning-template access.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin authenticates -> assigned admin profile is evaluated -> Device Manager/managed-device configuration areas are exposed read/write/read-only/none -> provisioning template or device change is authorized -> installation/push proceeds subject to device and package state.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Role-scope mismatch: administrator can access a device but cannot change/push a specific configuration area.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Admin profile permission matrix; GUI section visibility/editability; CLI profile fields device-interface/device-log/device-fabric/device-route/device-wan-link-load-balance; community report of custom admin unable to push FortiSwitch config.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Compare working and failing profiles per permission area; inspect the exact device configuration domain; explicitly set required permissions; retest least privilege; review upgrade migration because new sub-permissions default to None in existing custom profiles.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Identify which granular permission controls interface/DHCP, routing, log/report, and SD-WAN access after upgrade.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Administrator -> admin profile permission matrix -> Device Manager configuration domains -> install/push action; show read/write/none gates.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Anomaly Login Report: FortiAuthenticator event ingestion, ZTNA alert-handler dependency, and report object chain
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Recent: published last month; describes 10-15 minute post-reboot status lag
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Global Anomaly Login Report evaluates ZTNA remote-user/device behavior and depends on FortiAuthenticator event logs triggering the predefined ZTNA Login Anomaly Detection alert handler; report template, charts, macros, and dataset are separate report objects.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator emits event -> FortiAnalyzer receives/normalizes event -> predefined ZTNA Login Anomaly Detection alert handler fires -> incident/report dataset is populated -> global report renders from template/charts/macros.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Missing or delayed evidence pipeline causing an empty/incomplete anomaly report or false assumption of no suspicious activity.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Confirm FAC event logs are present; verify alert-handler trigger; inspect incident-Anomaly-Login dataset and report template/charts/macros; after reboot compare FortiGate OFTP connectivity, oftpd device listing, and fortilogd lograte before trusting stale GUI Last Log time.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Restore FAC event forwarding and alert-handler prerequisites; validate dataset and report objects; allow the documented 10-15 minute GUI refresh window after FAZ reboot; investigate network/authorization/fortilogd only if stale beyond 30 minutes.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Trace an empty anomaly report to missing FAC event/alert-handler prerequisites versus post-reboot GUI freshness lag.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator event source -> FortiAnalyzer ingestion -> ZTNA alert handler -> incident dataset -> report template/charts/macros -> analyst.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSwitchOS 8.0 DNS cache limit changes from entry count to memory budget
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: No directly matched recent Community scenario found in the 30-day sweep; feature lesson is documentation-driven.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: config system dns dns-cache-limit is a KB memory ceiling (1-1023 KB, default 512 KB) in FortiSwitchOS 8.0; prior releases interpreted it as maximum cache entry count (default 5000); dns-cache-ttl independently controls age.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Switch resolver receives query -> cache lookup -> miss sent to configured DNS server over cleartext or DoT -> response stored subject to TTL and memory cap -> dependent switch services reuse cached result.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Upgrade semantic mismatch: an old entry-count value is reinterpreted as a KB memory budget, causing unexpectedly small or large cache capacity.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Compare firmware version and `show system dns`; inspect dns-cache-limit and dns-cache-ttl separately; verify resolver reachability and whether affected switch functions (email alerts/URL blocking) are failing name resolution.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Recalculate dns-cache-limit as KB for 8.0; set an explicit memory budget within 1-1023 KB; preserve intended TTL and cache-notfound behavior; validate DNS server transport independently from cache capacity.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish DNS transport/TLS failure from cache eviction caused by the 8.0 unit change.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch resolver -> cache memory/TTL gate -> primary/secondary DNS server; annotate old entries vs new KB interpretation.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: CAPWAP control-channel DTLS trust and FortiAP join-state failure
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Recent: published last month; trace shows SULKING/DTLS_SETUP loop and certificate error
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: CAPWAP control channel is always protected by DTLS; the data channel is separately selectable as clear-text, DTLS, or IPsec. Control-channel certificate trust failure can prevent join before data-channel policy is relevant.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiAP discovers controller -> CAPWAP control-channel DTLS handshake and certificate validation -> AP authorization/profile assignment -> data channel established with profile-selected clear-text/DTLS/IPsec protection.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Control-channel DTLS certificate-chain trust failure causing repeated SULKING/DTLS_SETUP and AP remaining offline.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: `wcfg | grep fsm-state` oscillates through SULKING/DTLS_SETUP; AP debug reports `cwDtlsCertVerify` and self-signed certificate in chain; `cw_diag -c cert Fortinet_CA1.cer` returns no certificate output in the reported case.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Check the AP model/firmware and controller certificate chain; validate the required Fortinet CA certificate exists on the AP; apply the Fortinet-recommended fixed AP build/GA firmware; only after join, separately validate data-channel dtls-policy and performance impact.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Separate a CAPWAP control-channel certificate trust failure from a data-channel encryption-policy mismatch.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAP discovery -> DTLS control-channel certificate validation -> authorization/profile -> optional encrypted data channel; mark trust failure before authorization.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 Kerberos authentication for administrators and users
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Historical scenario (Feb 19, 2024), not a recent 30-day item; used only as context for keytab/domain-join distinction.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC 9.4 adds Kerberos for admin and user authentication on FortiNAC-CA and admin authentication on FNAC-M; LDAP directory configuration NetBIOS name selects Kerberos and must match a configured Winbind domain NetBIOS name.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User/admin submits credentials -> FortiNAC resolves configured LDAP directory and domain NetBIOS mapping -> Winbind/Kerberos realm validates against domain controller -> FortiNAC grants application role; domain join/keytab is a separate prerequisite path for Winbind-dependent flows.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Authentication-method mismatch: Kerberos is selected but NetBIOS/realm/Winbind mapping or domain join is inconsistent.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Check LDAP directory NetBIOS name, Winbind domain NetBIOS name, Kerberos realm, DC hostname, and Winbind status; compare authentication failure across admin/user surfaces and CA vs Manager.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Align domain NetBIOS and Kerberos realm values; ensure Winbind instance and domain join are healthy; use keytab where supported rather than storing a join-account password; validate each supported authentication surface separately.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Determine why a valid LDAP user fails Kerberos when the LDAP NetBIOS name does not match the Winbind instance.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin/user -> FortiNAC CA or Manager -> LDAP directory identity selection -> Winbind/Kerberos realm -> AD domain controller.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F LDAP signing enforcement: why TCP/389 simple binds fail and how LDAPS or STARTTLS restores secure directory access
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Very recent: published Nov 20, 2026 (one day before run)
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F directory connection supports Security Protocol None, SSL, and STARTTLS; TCP/389 simple bind without TLS is rejected by AD domain controllers enforcing LDAP signing; TLS-protected simple binds are accepted while signing enforcement remains enabled.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F opens LDAP TCP session -> sends simple bind over cleartext 389 or upgrades with StartTLS/starts LDAPS 636 -> DC evaluates LDAP signing/TLS requirement -> bind and credential validation -> directory synchronization and user/host mapping.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Directory bind security-policy mismatch: Active Directory rejects cleartext simple bind with Strong(er) authentication required when LDAP signing is required.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Community case reports Validate Credentials failing for every account; `openssl s_client -connect dc01.example.local:636 -showcerts` validates LDAPS certificate presentation; FortiNAC directory Security Protocol must be SSL/STARTTLS, Name must match certificate FQDN, Connect by Name should be enabled; Validate Credentials and subsequent directory sync succeed.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Keep AD LDAP signing requirement enabled; configure FortiNAC-F for LDAPS TCP/636 or STARTTLS TCP/389; install issuing CA in FortiNAC keystore under `/bsc/campusMgr/`; use the directory FQDN and Connect by Name; validate credentials and directory synchronization; avoid weakening domain-controller signing policy except as a temporary approved workaround.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Choose the secure fix for FortiNAC-F simple-bind rejection by an AD domain controller requiring LDAP signing, distinguishing TCP/389 cleartext from STARTTLS and LDAPS.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F LDAP client -> TCP/389 cleartext rejected branch vs STARTTLS upgrade/TCP/636 LDAPS trusted TLS branch -> Active Directory DC -> credential validation/synchronization.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: OAuth IAM login and OIDC claims: identity-source selection and remote-LDAP user failure boundary
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Recent: published Nov 16, 2026 (5 days before run)
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator 6.6 adds IAM as an OAuth policy identity source and IAM account/user OIDC claims on Authorization Code (with/without PKCE); OAuth policy identity sources and relying-party claim selection determine identity and token attributes.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client redirects to /oauth/authorize -> policy portal and identity source authenticate IAM or configured user -> relying party authorization code issued -> client exchanges code at /oauth/token -> OIDC claims returned according to relying-party configuration.
selected_candidates.failure_class: OAuth authorization endpoint exception for non-imported remote LDAP user in 6.6.10 (`RemoteLdapSessionUser` lacks fac_groups), not a generic OIDC protocol failure.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: HTTP 500 at `/api/v1/oauth/authorize/`; traceback `AttributeError: 'RemoteLdapSessionUser' object has no attribute 'fac_groups'`; affected version 6.6.10; fixed in 6.6.12 and 8.0.5.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Confirm identity source and remote-user import state; do not misdiagnose as redirect URI/client-secret failure; upgrade to 6.6.12 or 8.0.5 or later fixed build; validate authorization-code and token exchange with imported and non-imported user cases.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Identify a server-side remote LDAP user object failure from HTTP 500 and select the fixed-build remediation rather than changing OAuth client parameters.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: OIDC client -> FortiAuthenticator OAuth policy/identity source -> authorization code -> token endpoint -> relying-party claims; show non-imported remote LDAP branch.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiPAM 1.9 launcher process matcher: window-title and command-line identity with mandatory recording
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Historical scenario (Mar 11, 2026), not a recent 30-day item; used only to distinguish launcher TLS transport from process matching.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 identifies the main process by Default, Regex on GUI Window Title, or Regex on Command Line; non-default matchers force Multiprocess Mode and Full-screen Recording.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User launches secret -> FortiClient launcher starts application/process tree -> matcher finds target process/window -> full-screen recording captures session context across child processes -> audit trail associates activity with managed secret session.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Launcher process selection/audit coverage failure for Java apps, IDEs, child-process launchers, or changing window titles.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Matcher type and regex pattern in `config os_app`; `multipleprocess enable` and `fullscreen-record enable` required when custom matcher is used; test application spawn tree and recording output.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Choose stable window-title or command-line regex; test against real process arguments/title changes; keep multiprocess and full-screen recording enabled; do not confuse endpoint TLS trust errors with matcher selection.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Select the correct matcher and mandatory audit settings when a Java application spawns child processes and changes its window title.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM secret -> FortiClient launcher -> parent/child process tree -> regex matcher -> full-screen recording/audit stream.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM 7.4 rule tags: taxonomy attached to rule actions and searchable incidents/cases
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: No directly matched recent Community scenario found in the 30-day sweep; feature lesson is documentation-driven.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: System-defined tags are linked to built-in rules; user-defined tags are created under Admin > Settings > Analytics > Rule Tags and attached in rule Step 3 Define Actions; active tags surface on incident/case lists and search.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Event matches correlation rule -> rule action emits incident with configured tags -> incident/case list and sidebar expose tags -> analysts filter rules/incidents/cases by tag.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Classification/search gap: tag exists but is not associated with the triggering rule, or an analyst searches the wrong tag field/scope.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Rule Tags Scope column distinguishes System vs User; rule editor Tag field; Incident/Case Tag column and sidebar; search syntax uses Incident Tag for incidents and Tag for cases.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Create or verify tag, attach it to the intended rule action, confirm rule save/activation, generate a test incident, then verify list column/sidebar/search; do not attempt to delete system tags.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Trace a missing incident tag to rule-action association rather than parser or event-ingestion failure.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Event -> correlation rule -> tag association -> incident/case record -> list/sidebar/search.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: Branch On-ramp architecture: IPsec branch aggregation, FWaaS policy, BGP-per-overlay versus static routing
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: Historical scenario (Jun 29, 2026), not a recent 30-day item; documents third-party IPsec parameter alignment.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Branch On-ramp terminates IPsec from one or more branch devices at a FortiSASE security PoP; branch device centralizes remote-user traffic to FWaaS; endpoints use the branch device as default gateway; BGP-per-overlay exposes individual client source IPs, while static routing requires source NAT for return traffic.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Branch IPsec device establishes tunnel to PoP -> BGP per overlay or static/SNAT route design advertises/returns branch prefixes -> FortiSASE profile groups and policies inspect traffic -> return traffic follows learned or translated path.
selected_candidates.failure_class: On-ramp tunnel established but branch routes/return path or subscription capacity prevents usable FWaaS access.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Verify tunnel phase1/phase2 and byte counters; inspect BGP neighbor per overlay and learned routes; distinguish client source IP visibility with BGP from tunnel-IP visibility with static+SNAT; validate license seats, locations, and data-transfer allowance.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Configure SPA network/BGP settings before deploying On-ramp; choose BGP per overlay when preserving client IP visibility; if static routing is used, source-NAT traffic on the branch device; align IKE/PSK/peer IDs; verify license and PoP capacity.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Choose BGP per-overlay versus static+SNAT based on whether FortiSASE must see the original client source IP.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Multiple branch LANs -> branch IPsec edge -> FortiSASE On-ramp PoP/FWaaS -> internet/private destinations; annotate BGP-per-overlay return path vs static+SNAT.

selected_candidates.lesson_subject: ToS-based SD-WAN packet duplication and de-duplication matching
selected_candidates.scenario_age_status: No directly matched recent Community scenario found in the 30-day sweep; feature lesson is documentation-driven.
selected_candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 adds ToS match and ToS mask to config system sdwan config duplication; duplication/de-duplication rules match the 8-bit ToS field after mask application, allowing selective replicated traffic.
selected_candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Ingress packet classified by source/destination/service/interface and ToS mask -> source FortiGate duplication rule replicates matching packet across selected SD-WAN zone members -> remote FortiGate de-duplication rule matches same traffic/ToS and suppresses duplicates.
selected_candidates.failure_class: Duplicate traffic not created or not suppressed because ToS byte/mask, zone members, direction, or matching rule differs between endpoints.
selected_candidates.evidence_pattern: Compare `set tos` and `set tos-mask` on both ends; test ToS 0x77 versus 0x00; expected behavior is no duplication for 0x00 and duplicate/de-duplicate only for 0x77; verify IPv4 and IPv6 separately.
selected_candidates.remediation_path: Use identical ToS value and mask on duplication/de-duplication sides; verify packet marking at source; validate zones and service/address selectors; avoid broad masks unless intentionally matching multiple classes.
selected_candidates.question_fingerprint: Calculate whether a packet matches a ToS/mask rule and diagnose asymmetric duplicate/de-duplicate behavior.
selected_candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Source FortiGate with SD-WAN zone and duplication fan-out -> multiple overlay paths -> remote FortiGate with matching de-duplication rule -> single forwarded packet.

selection_notes: FortiAP FQDN Layer 3 ACL rejected because the 30-day inventory already contains that mechanism (2026-11-13).
FortiPAM Multiple Target Address rejected because it was taught on 2026-11-12.
FortiAuthenticator CMPv2 retained as a discovery candidate but replaced with OAuth IAM/OIDC identity-source behavior because a current 6.6.10 OAuth failure was found in Community.
FortiGate DHCP templates replaced with a recent proxy-mode deep-inspection/ALPN case supported by Fortinet proxy SSL-inspection and web-proxy documentation.
FortiSwitch DNS cache limit is deliberately separated from the recent DoT trust-validation lesson: the subject is the 8.0 change from entry count to KB memory budget, not transport encryption.

FortiNAC-F N+1 failover was retained as a high-value Community sweep finding but not selected as the primary lesson; the Nov 20 LDAP-signing failure offered a more recent, directly actionable scenario with matching official LDAP connection settings.

additional_recent_community_findings.finding: N+1 upgrade sequencing and missing primary CA entries in Manager Server List; retained as secondary sweep finding.
